descriptor.scene: Two people fill the middle of the frame from the waist up: Gary and Maya, walking slowly together down the hall of framed doors, deep in it now. Gary counts on his fingers, three fingers up, making the third point; Maya watches his hands, nodding, working it through. The framed, spotlit doors recede behind them soft and out of focus, their plaques too small to read. Warm museum light.
negatives: readable plaque text anywhere in this image
descriptor._caption: The guide says the doors follow three rules. A door opens when something newly built makes a new kind of company possible. It closes as the obvious things get made. And while it is open, it never looks important. That is why founders call them windows.
